newsitem.title: UK: Iraq May Kirkuk export schedule sees slight rise.
newsitem.headline: Iraq May Kirkuk export schedule sees slight rise.

text.p: Iraq has set a preliminary schedule for May Kirkuk crude exports of 445,000 barrels a day (bpd), up a little from an original programme 430,000 bpd programme for April, traders said on Wednesday.
May exports of Kirkuk from Iraq's Turkish pipeline outlet at Ceyhan on the Mediterranean are expected to total 13.78 million barrels in 15 cargoes.

Full Iraqi exports under the U.N.'s humanitarian oil sale in recent weeks have been running at some 750,000 bpd, with the remainder made up of sales of Basrah Light from Iraq's Gulf terminal Mina al-Bakr.
Traders said most May Kirkuk cargoes already were committed.
A May 10-20 cargo was offered at a 40-50 cent premium to the Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organisation's (SOMO) official price of Dated Brent less $2.20 a barrel fob Ceyhan.
Kirkuk has traded at some 25 cents a barrel over the official May price, at Dated Brent less $1.95, after a swift turnaround in refining margins over the past few weeks.

"The (refining) margins are very good but that is too expensive for me," one Spanish refiner said of Wednesday's Kirkuk offer. Traders said the Kirkuk seller would now be most likely to take the cargo into its own refining system.
